A campaign I'm proud of

Themed Rooms:
a bedroom worth sharing

Five rooms, four channels, one story. A student accommodation campaign for international students, the same audience Warwick Business School recruits.

Start with a question

Jackie Su · Digital Communications Executive (Social Media) · Warwick Business School interview, 16 October 2026

Before we start

Which room would you pick?

Choose one. Then see how international students answered the same question.

Share of themed-room enquiries

Gaming and Zodiac were the first rooms to be fully booked.

The brief

Get more students seeing, and talking about, our brand

The goal

Brand exposure and engagement

More reach, and more people interacting with us, ahead of the booking season.

The problem

Every student room looks the same

Bed, desk, wardrobe. Our posts got a steady few hundred views and blended into every other listing.

The audience

International students, choosing from photos

Most decide from abroad, months ahead, often with their parents.

Research first

Students chose the themes, and the data refined them

Ten themes tested
GamingPlantsDollsInstagramZodiacBasketballFlowersStarry skyPetsAnime

Asked online, at our Freshers' Fair stand, and face to face.

Can we run it?
  • Cost to fit out
  • Easy to reset between tenants
  • Safe and allowed in the building
  • Looks good in photos and video
Top five built
  1. Gaming room
  2. Aesthetic room
  3. Wonderland room
  4. Instagram room
  5. Zodiac room

Phase 1 (2022) launched with Esports, NBA, plants and dolls. Feedback and enquiry data shaped this final five.

The 5Cs

One word per room, one kind of student

Compete

Gaming room

For gamers and streamers who want their setup ready on day one

Calm

Aesthetic room

For students who want a quiet, green space to study and switch off

Comfort

Wonderland room

For first-years far from home who want somewhere soft to land

Create

Instagram room

For content creators who want every corner camera-ready

Connect

Zodiac room

For social students who love a "which one are you?" conversation

Room visuals redrawn in one style, based on the original design boards.

From board to room

Every room started as a design board

One board, two jobs: a shopping list for the operations team, and ready-made content for social.

Original design board, Gaming room.

Four channels

One story, told differently on each platform

The deep read

WeChat Official Account

Longer articles, room by room, for students and parents in China: the render, every item, and the price (£550 for the Gaming room), so parents can decide too.

On launch day I asked six site teams to repost it on their own channels.

Original WeChat article (in Chinese).

Discovery

Xiaohongshu

Searchable notes with strong covers. On Xiaohongshu people search first and save for later, so a note travels when people save it.

This post: 1,564 views against a usual 800 to 900, 165 likes and 23 enquiries.

Launch day, 1 June 2022: the article shared with six site teams to repost.

The look

Instagram and TikTok

Carousels and short video for students already in the UK. The cover asks a question, "Which room are you?", because a question gets comments and shares; a list doesn't.

Instagram post, mock-up recreated for this presentation.

Where interest lands

Official website

A themed-rooms page with the enquiry and viewing form. At checkout, students add a theme under "Additional services".

Original booking page (first-phase themes shown).

Working with others

It travelled because other people carried it

Sales team

Briefed before launch, ready for the enquiry spike.

Operations team

Built the rooms and kept them ready for viewings.

Universities, agents, ambassadors

Shared through student channels, used with agents' clients, reposted to ambassadors' own followers.

Local suppliers

Featured in our posts, in return for better prices, so the budget went further.

Results

Views roughly doubled or better on every channel

+10%website page views in the launch month
+15%time spent on the booking page
12%of that month's enquiries were about themed rooms

"Usual" is the typical range for our regular posts on that channel; bars show its midpoint. Bars in each view are drawn to one scale.

From post to booking

A short path from interest to a paid add-on

1 · Join

A WeChat interest group kept leads warm until booking opened. (QR code blurred.)

2 · Book and add a theme

On the website, the theme is added at checkout.

3 · Revenue£400–550

per room, sold as a paid add-on. "Only a few left" on every post gave people a reason to book now. The campaign created a new revenue line, not only reach.

What I'd do differently

A spike is a start, not a result

Plan the follow-up

Attention fades in days. I'd have a series ready, one room a week, to hold it.

Track through to bookings

Tag every enquiry by source, so I can show which channel turned interest into tenancies.

Put more into TikTok

It brought the most enquiries (35). The follow-up series would have started there.

What this means for WBS

Find what's worth sharing, then help the right people share it

A story, not a prospectus

The spaces, people and moments students actually want to post about.

Shaped for each platform

Including Xiaohongshu and WeChat, where many applicants decide from abroad.

Ambassadors as partners

Briefed early, with a kit, and measured on enquiries as well as reach.

One idea for WBS"Which WBS student are you?"

Five programmes, five kinds of student, voted on by ambassadors.
